text.tspan: How to think about standard deviation
: Something that is always the same, like an
Oreo cookie, has no variation. If you were to measure weights, calories, or anything else
in a sample of Oreo cookies, the standard deviation would be close to zero. Oreo cookies
consistent. On the other hand, Grandma Dee’s famous homemade cookies varied
quite a bit. They were made from scratch in small batches and were not always consistent.
Some were smaller, some larger, some had more chocolate chips, some had fewer calories,
etc. So, the standard deviation for measurements of Grandma Dee’s homemade cookies
would be larger, due to the variation. They were less consistent (but delicious!).
Here are the definitions of population variance and population standard deviation. Throughout most of
the book we will focus on standard deviation as a measure of variation and leave the study of variance
until later. However, the two are closely related so both are presented here. Also, keep in mind
